item.name: Slang GPU shaders (.slang, .slangh)
item.target_level: L2 proposed; higher levels only if an independent native oracle proves them

order: G-R1 OpenCL precedes Slang. Controller currently authorizes triage only; NP-Q5 (how many language lanes to keep) must be answered before implementation.
implemented_behavior: None. No dialect, grammar lock/blob, classification map, canonical corpus, reading or generated tracker change.
oracle_tiers: Unassigned until output and context validation. Reconstructed compiler invocations cap at tier B. Native semantic output needs actual untranslated subject context and coverage proof for tier A; a native binary name alone gives no tier upgrade. Same-grammar queries cap at tier C.
method: Prefer official Slang declaration/reflection/source-location API, AST dump and AST-backed slangd navigation; qualify end ranges, written call sites and resolved import edges before adapter work. Reuse existing langbench schema/scope/tier rules; no new runtime service. Runtime coverage is executed subset only.
activation: Controller owns canonical queue/plan rows. This proposal changes neither.
population_status: Metadata only: all 466 candidates have dispositions, with 48 eligible whole projects. Primary: 47 projects, 2,752 files and 14,417,219 bytes. Separate Falcor holdout: 461 files and 2,951,994 bytes. All 18 old pins and 22 previously verified new pins remain fixed. Per-file license terms and checkout fidelity remain admission checks; no measurements.
future_gate: Primary and holdout must separately meet at most 5% ERROR-or-MISSING files and at most 0.1% faults on the same frozen grammar revision. Report both; the weaker group caps any level or change note.
search_boundary: Complete ParameterBlock and four README/topic repository queries, plus earlier queries, named seeds and all historical discoveries. GitHub allowed 10 code requests per minute. No r3a shader-attribute requests followed. The reported total is search output, not a verified count of real attributes. This bounded discovery is neither reach-complete nor an atomic snapshot.
